GET /api/v1/compendium/cards/{card_id}/r.description: The card as printed. `format=json` gives the render model (every value on the card, translated); `lang` picks the language of every text on the card (name, description, country, region, type, rarity, difficulty, labels). A text that is empty in that language is taken from the next language that has one (en, de, pl in this order), first from the card, then from the POI. `ratio` is the shape of the card as width:height (default 63:88, the trading card; also 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 3:2, 16:9, ...), whole numbers 1 to 100, between 2:5 and 5:2. From 13:10 on the photo moves to the left of the texts. The shorter side is always 63 mm, so text keeps its size. `style` is the look of the card: `standard` (default) or `3d` (raised frame, glass panels, holographic sheen); any other name answers 422. `dpi` is the sharpness of a `png` or `jpg`, 72 to 2000 (default 300: 815 x 1110 px on 63:88; `dpi=600` is twice as wide and high). The file records it, so a print program knows the size. A wide or tall shape has more pixels at the same dpi, so very high values answer 422 with the highest dpi that fits. It is ignored for `svg`, `pdf` and `json`. Only 63:88 in the standard style at 300 dpi is stored by the render job; other ratios, styles and dpi are drawn on request. Any other parameter answers 422. `svg`, `png` (300 dpi), `jpg` (300 dpi) and `pdf` give the file with 3 mm bleed in the rarity colour. Files made by the render job are served when they are up to date, otherwise the card is drawn now. `download=true` asks the browser to save the file.

POST /api/v1/assets/icons/link.description: Sets `icon_id` on every row that has none yet and whose icon text (the 19 reference tables and the resource types: the old `icon` column in lower case), ISO code (countries: the icon `flag_<iso code>`, for example `flag_at`) or ISO 3166-2 code (regions: `flag_ch_zh`) matches the **key** of an icon. The API version of `scripts/sql/icons_link.sql`. A link that is already set is never changed, so it can be run again after every import. The answer says how many rows were linked per table and how many still have no icon (no icon with their key exists yet). `dry_run=true` counts without saving. Needs the update permission on reference data (administrator by default). These bulk updates are not written to the event log one by one.

POST /api/v1/assets/icons/upload-csv.description:
Multipart form with a CSV in `file` (UTF-8, comma separated, the first row is the header; at most ICON_CSV_MAX_UPLOAD_MB, default 5 MB, and ICON_CSV_MAX_ROWS, default 2000 rows). Columns: `key` and `svg` (required), `name`, `name_de`, `name_pl`, `summary`, `summary_de`, `summary_pl` (optional; `name` defaults to the key). `scripts/make_icon_set.py` makes such a file (`icons_import.csv`). Every SVG is cleaned like an upload (what was taken out is in `notes`); a wrong row (bad key, key twice, not an SVG) is skipped and named in `errors`, the other rows are used.

- `dry_run=true`: everything is checked and counted, nothing is saved. Use it first.
- `update=true`: an icon whose key exists is replaced (SVG and names) when it differs; without it, existing icons are left alone (`unchanged`). Needs the update permission on icons.
- `link=true` (default): afterwards every row whose icon text (reference tables, resource types), ISO code (countries, flag_xx) or ISO 3166-2 code (regions) matches the key of an icon gets its `icon_id`, as `POST /assets/icons/link` does. Needs the update permission on reference data; use `link=false` to skip it.

Administrator only by default. The answer says how many icons were created, replaced, left alone and rejected, and what was linked.
